page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The products
lines: Diborane B₂H₆ is hydrolysed by water.
Each boron ends up bonded to three OH
The hydrogen of the diborane leaves as
steps.why: Water supplies OH to boron and H⁺ to the hydride hydrogen. The hydride H of diborane and the H⁺ of water combine and leave as hydrogen gas, and boron is left as orthoboric acid, which is also written B(OH)₃.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the hydrogen gas. Hydrolysis of diborane releases H₂ as well as the acid.
Giving boric oxide B₂O₃ as the product. B₂O₃ comes from heating the acid, not from hydrolysis.
steps.memory_tip: Two borons give two H₃BO₃, and the six hydride hydrogens leave as H₂.
steps.margin_note: H₃BO₃ may also be written B(OH)₃; both forms are correct.

steps.label: The balanced equation
lines: Two boron atoms need two H₃BO₃, and those
take six oxygen atoms from six waters.
steps.why: Six water molecules carry the six oxygen atoms that the two H₃BO₃ molecules need. Counting hydrogen last confirms the equation: 6 from B₂H₆ plus 12 from the water on the left, and 6 in the acid plus 12 in the hydrogen gas on the right.
common_mistakes: Writing 3H₂O. Six water molecules are needed, one for each oxygen atom in the two acid molecules.
Writing 3H₂ instead of 6H₂. Six molecules of hydrogen gas are released.
steps.memory_tip: Count oxygen first: two H₃BO₃ need six O, so six H₂O.
steps.margin_note: Show the hydrogen count, since that is where the balance is checked.

insider_note: Both products carry the answer, so write H₃BO₃ and H₂ together with their coefficients rather than the acid alone.
